function: CSI feedback for FDD massive MIMO: autoencoder compression and recovery of CSI, trained with GAN-synthesized CSI via gossip learning; generative replay against catastrophic forgetting in new areas (pp. 3-7).
system: FDD massive MIMO-OFDM downlink, BS with 32 antennas, single-antenna UEs, 32 subcarriers, 25 paths, 0.05 GHz bandwidth; DeepMIMO O1_28 outdoor scenario at 28 GHz; no RIS (pp. 3, 8).
method: CsiNet autoencoder trained on CSI synthesized by a consistency-regularized Wasserstein GAN; GAN trained by decentralized gossip learning (D2D model averaging, K=10 UEs, 500 CSI each); generative replay (pp. 3-8).
data_channel: DeepMIMO O1_28 ray tracing, dense (BS15) and sparse (BS4) areas, 10,000 samples each, 5,000 train and 5,000 test; COST2100 indoor 5.3 GHz used for loss comparison (p. 8).
test_conditions: 5,000/5,000 train/test split within an area; Table VI tests sparse-trained models on the dense area and vice versa, with and without retraining or generative replay (pp. 8, 12).
baselines: Learned only: centralized GAN, unconnected GANs, FL-trained CsiNet, Sync D&G federated GAN, true-CSI CsiNet, retraining; no non-learned baseline such as CS or codebook (pp. 8-9, 12).
metrics: NMSE (dB) with 95% confidence intervals and loss variance; FLOPs, memory and per-epoch time; NMSE versus fake-data size, compression ratio, number of UEs, and encoder architecture (pp. 8-12).
complexity: Order O(NtNc + npeers K T log(NtNc)) (p. 8); Table IV: 0.98T FLOPs, 7.142M memory, 2.977 s per epoch versus 9.8T, 42.296M, 25.784 s for centralized GAN (p. 9).
openness: none released by the authors; uses public DeepMIMO (https://www.deepmimo.net/, p. 3) and COST2100 datasets (p. 8).
q1_support: p. 3: "3D ray-tracing parameters are generated via DeepMIMO"
q2_support: p. 12: "The NMSE performance when the UE moves from a sparse area to a dense area"
q3_support: p. 8: "We compare the NMSE performance of our proposed Gossip-GAN framework with three counterparts" (all counterparts are learned; compressed sensing and codebook schemes appear only as background on p. 1, no non-learned baseline is compared)
q4_support: p. 8: "the computational complexity order of the GAN training is O(Nt Nc )"
q5_support: p. 8: "DeepMIMO is a publicly available dataset generated by the Remcom Wireless Insite tool"
notes: PDF is arXiv 2509.10490v1; its title and authors match the Crossref record of this DOI (checked outside the PDF). The text layer of pp. 9-13 holds only garbled figure labels, so pp. 9-13 were read from page images (Fig. 8 and Table IV on p. 9, Table VI on p. 12). Area 2: the learned parts are a CSI feedback autoencoder and a GAN that synthesizes CSI; gossip learning is D2D model averaging, not over-the-air aggregation, so not area 7. q1: DeepMIMO ray tracing (p. 3); COST2100 also appears in Table III (p. 8). q2: Table VI (p. 12) reports the sparse-trained CsiNet tested on the dense area (-0.54 dB, no retraining; p. 11 says it performs poorly in new scenarios) and the retraining and generative-replay results; a direct cross-area test counts. q3: counterparts in Figs. 8, 9, 11 and Table VI are the true-CSI CsiNet, centralized GAN, unconnected GANs, FL-trained CsiNet and Sync D&G federated GAN; none is non-learned. q4: the reported cost is that of GAN training (order, FLOPs, memory, per-epoch time), not of encoder inference. Fig. 9 labels the dense and sparse areas the other way round from Fig. 8 and Table V.
